JPM.rationale: JPM's fundamental health and trajectory are genuinely strong: Q1 2026 revenue of $49.84B (+10% YoY), EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY), operating margin of 39.9%, and ROE of 16.2% all reflect a franchise firing on all cylinders. Q2 2026 results (reported 2026-07-22) were even stronger — $58B managed revenue, $16.9B net income ex-significant items ($6.14 EPS), with raised full-year NII guidance to ~$105.5B. The franchise is elite: 8.4% global IB fee share, $5.1T AUM, dominant deposit and payments positions, and a $19.9B technology budget that no peer can match. However, valuation has already re-rated significantly — P/E moved from 13.9x in May to 16.16x currently, near the upper quartile of its 365-day range (13.7–17.8), and P/B at 2.615x is elevated for a bank. The stock is at $349.90, near its 365-day high of $351.24, having absorbed much of the Q1 beat. Incorporating Q2's $6.14 EPS improves the trailing earnings picture, but the market has already moved. The near-term catalyst is the Q2 earnings beat and raised guidance (reported 2026-07-22), which provides modest support, but Dimon's own caution that results were 'supercharged by one-time events' and the hawkish Fed pivot temper enthusiasm. Persistent negative operating cash flow and expanding leverage (assets/equity from 12.4x to 13.5x) add balance-sheet caution. On balance: excellent franchise, good trajectory, but fair-to-slightly-rich valuation limits upside from here. Score of +0.35 reflects strong fundamentals capped by limited valuation cushion.
